answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a developer-centric, implementation details matter register, it stays short. The design leans on recursive zk-SNARKs for scalable verification. The sable holds work receipts rather than names, so the jade of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Reaching the vertex of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
